newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels kill 17 Algerians - papers.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels kill 17 Algerians - papers.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas have killed 17 Algerian civilians by cutting their throats, bringing to nearly 100 the number slaughtered in a four-day wave of renewed violence, Algerian newspapers said on Monday.

Fifteen people were killed in a Moslem rebel raid in Tiaret province, 225 km (140 miles) southwest of Algiers. Their bodies were found late on Sunday near the small town of Ain el Hadid in Tiaret area, said Liberte newspaper.
The newspaper gave no more details about the killings but said that 13 shepherds had also been abducted by Moslem rebels on Saturday from a forest near el Gaada village in the same province.
Livestock is the main economic activity in Tiaret area in Algeria's highlands.
In another incident, a local Moslem religious leader and his nephew were killed, their throats cut, in Saida, 340 km (210 miles)) southwest of Algiers last week, said El Watan newspaper.
The unnamed religious figure was the leader of the local Sidi Abdelkrim shrine, it added.
Moslem guerrillas have killed several hundred Moslem religious officials they accuse of supporting the government's moderate Islamic approach.

During the past Algerian weekend of Thursday and Friday, Moslem rebels massacred more than 80 villagers in several areas of Algeria, killing some with chainsaws and dousing others in burning petrol, Algerian newspapers reported on Sunday.

The North African country has been without an elected parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead. About 60,000 people have been killed since then in violence pitting guerrillas against government forces.
